title: RBRA Vessel Buy-Back - payment, fund charged, receipts, grant claims and ownership records (incl. Malcolm Aug 19, 2022 statement) for CF 5286 TX and floating home CF 3944 TZ

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request is directed to the County of Marin, including the Department of Finance, the County Administrator's Office (Budget Office), the Department of Public Works, and the County-employed staff of the Richardson Bay Regional Agency (RBRA), whose budget the County administers and whose payments the County processes. It concerns two vessels RBRA acquired under its Vessel Buy-Back Program and then removed and demolished:

- Vessel 1 - CF 5286 TX, 1986 Starfire 26-ft powerboat, HIN SRFK3514A686. Acquired by RBRA on August 19, 2022 (Holly Wild); removed to the Army Corps of Engineers yard in Sausalito the same day; demolished on or about August 24, 2022 by Tim Nunes Tracks (Invoice No. 2022-550, $1,102.50).

- Vessel 2 - CF 3944 TZ, 60-ft floating home (registered owner Larry Moyer, deceased 2016), with three associated small motor vessels. Acquired by RBRA under a General Release and Compromise Agreement and a Supplemental Agreement dated February 27, 2024, for a total of $22,500 paid through MarinLink check requests of $13,400 (Feb. 27, 2024), $5,700 (Mar. 6, 2024) and $3,400 (Apr. 23, 2024); removed from the anchorage February 28, 2024 and disposed of thereafter.

Period: June 1, 2022 to the present. I request:

1. All financial records of each acquisition, including the buy-back agreement and any supplemental agreement, MarinLink check requests, County claims, warrants, payment vouchers, and the fund, account, and project code charged (including whether fund 8050 / project 40RBRAEPA, County one-time funds, or any state or federal grant account) for every payment to the occupant or purported owner of either vessel.

2. All proof-of-ownership records for either vessel, including DMV Vehicle/Vessel Information Request printouts, bills of sale, releases of liability, text messages, statements of ownership, and affidavits, and specifically: (a) the written statement dated August 19, 2022 signed by RBRA Harbormaster James Malcolm concerning his conversation with the registered co-owner of Vessel 1 and the vessel's ownership; (b) the Statement of Ownership dated February 27, 2024 for Vessel 2; (c) the Affidavit of Ownership executed by Mr. Malcolm on February 26, 2025 for Vessel 2; and (d) any DMV record for Vessel 2 obtained in or after March 2021.

3. All receipts, invoices, and proofs of payment for the removal, transport, storage, and demolition of either vessel, including Tim Nunes Tracks Invoices 2022-547 through 2022-550 and all February-April 2024 contractor, Marin County Sheriff's Office, or Army Corps of Engineers charges for Vessel 2, with the account or grant to which each was charged.

4. All reimbursement claims submitted to the California Division of Boating and Waterways (SAVE, AWAF, or VTIP), NOAA (award NA21NOS9990023), or EPA (San Francisco Bay Water Quality Improvement Fund) that include any cost for either vessel, together with all attachments submitted with each claim.

5. All correspondence (including email of RBRA staff on marincounty.org accounts) among RBRA, MarinLink, the County, DBW, NOAA, or EPA mentioning "5286 TX," "5286TX," "Starfire," Holly Wild, Kyle or Kathleen Quayle, Brian Greenstein, "3944 TZ," "3944TZ," Moyer, "floating home," or the Vessel Buy-Back Program.

Please redact rather than withhold personal identifiers of private individuals, and identify any record withheld and the exemption claimed.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson

title: EPA SF Bay WQIF grant to RBRA - buyback, removal and disposal costs and ownership records for CF 5286 TX (Aug 2022) and floating home CF 3944 TZ (Feb 2024)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: EPA SF Bay WQIF grant to RBRA - buyback, removal and disposal costs and ownership records for CF 5286 TX (Aug 2022) and floating home CF 3944 TZ (Feb 2024)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request is directed to EPA Region 9 (San Francisco) and concerns the San Francisco Bay Water Quality Improvement Fund assistance agreement to the Richardson Bay Regional Agency (RBRA), a joint powers agency in Marin County, California (approximately $2,782,586; carried in RBRA's books as fund 8050, project 40RBRAEPA), as it relates to RBRA's Vessel Buy-Back Program and two vessels RBRA acquired under that program and then removed and demolished. RBRA's FY 2024-25 budget staff report states that "the EPA grant has additional reimbursable funds available" for the Buy-Back Program.

- Vessel 1 - CF 5286 TX, 1986 Starfire 26-ft powerboat, HIN SRFK3514A686. Acquired by RBRA on August 19, 2022 (Holly Wild); removed to the Army Corps of Engineers yard in Sausalito the same day; demolished on or about August 24, 2022 by Tim Nunes Tracks (Invoice No. 2022-550, $1,102.50).

- Vessel 2 - CF 3944 TZ, 60-ft floating home (registered owner Larry Moyer, deceased 2016), with three associated small motor vessels. Acquired by RBRA under agreements dated February 27, 2024 for a total of $22,500 paid through MarinLink check requests of $13,400, $5,700 and $3,400; removed from the anchorage February 28, 2024 and disposed of thereafter.

Period: January 1, 2022 to the present. I request:

1. The assistance agreement, work plan, approved budget, and all amendments, to the extent they describe vessel buy-back, vessel acquisition, vessel removal, or vessel disposal as eligible or reimbursable costs.

2. All payment requests, ASAP drawdowns, SF-425 financial reports, and supporting invoices, receipts, ledgers, or cost documentation submitted by RBRA that include any Vessel Buy-Back Program payment, any payment to MarinLink for buy-back purposes, the $22,500 paid for Vessel 2, or any removal, transport, storage, or disposal cost for Vessel 1 or Vessel 2.

3. All progress or performance reports and attachments submitted by RBRA that identify vessels acquired, removed, or disposed of under the agreement.

4. Any proof of ownership, DMV record, statement of ownership, affidavit, or written statement concerning either vessel provided to EPA, including the written statement dated August 19, 2022 signed by RBRA Harbormaster James Malcolm (Vessel 1), and the Statement of Ownership dated February 27, 2024 and the Affidavit of Ownership executed by Mr. Malcolm on February 26, 2025 (Vessel 2).

5. All correspondence between EPA and RBRA, the County of Marin, or the San Francisco Estuary Partnership mentioning the Vessel Buy-Back Program, "5286 TX," "Starfire," Holly Wild, "3944 TZ," Moyer, or "floating home."

I request a fee waiver: these records concern the expenditure of federal funds by a public agency, I am not seeking them for commercial use, and I intend to make them available to the public. If the waiver is denied, I agree to pay fees up to $25.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson

title: RBRA SAVE claims, attachments and ownership records for vessels CF 5286 TX (Aug 2022 buyback) and CF 3944 TZ floating home (Feb 2024 buyback)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: RBRA SAVE claims, attachments and ownership records for vessels CF 5286 TX (Aug 2022 buyback) and CF 3944 TZ floating home (Feb 2024 buyback)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request, directed to the Division of Boating and Waterways (DBW), concerns two vessels acquired by the Richardson Bay Regional Agency (RBRA) under its Vessel Buy-Back Program and subsequently removed and demolished:

- Vessel 1 - CF 5286 TX, 1986 Starfire 26-ft powerboat, HIN SRFK3514A686. Acquired by RBRA on August 19, 2022 (Holly Wild); removed to the Army Corps of Engineers yard in Sausalito the same day; demolished on or about August 24, 2022 by Tim Nunes Tracks (Invoice No. 2022-550, $1,102.50). RBRA listed this vessel by CF number in its SAVE FY 2022/23 grant application (Contract C22S0608, Exhibit F budget dated August 12, 2022, p. 42 of 44) under "Estimate Future Abandoned Vessels" at $4,000.

- Vessel 2 - CF 3944 TZ, 60-ft floating home (registered owner Larry Moyer, deceased 2016), with three associated small motor vessels. Acquired by RBRA under a General Release and Compromise Agreement and a Supplemental Agreement dated February 27, 2024, for a total of $22,500 paid through MarinLink check requests of $13,400 (Feb. 27, 2024), $5,700 (Mar. 6, 2024) and $3,400 (Apr. 23, 2024); removed from the anchorage February 28, 2024 and disposed of thereafter.

Period: June 1, 2022 to the present. Under SAVE agreements C21S0608 (FY 2021-22), C22S0608 (FY 2022-23), SAVE 23 (FY 2023-24), and any other SAVE, AWAF or VTIP agreement with RBRA or the County of Marin, I request:

1. Every reimbursement claim, DPR 264 (VTIP), DPR 265 (match), AWAF form, accounting spreadsheet, or other payment request that lists, includes, or was supported in whole or in part by costs for Vessel 1 or Vessel 2, including the claim(s) in which Tim Nunes Tracks Invoices 2022-549 and 2022-550 were submitted, and any claim for the February-March 2024 removal and disposal of Vessel 2.

2. All attachments and supporting documents submitted with each such claim, including contractor invoices, receipts, proofs of payment, photographs, DMV records, bills of sale, releases of liability, statements of ownership, affidavits, and any "ownership verified" certification for either vessel.

3. All proof-of-ownership or title-search records RBRA provided to DBW for either vessel, including any DMV Vehicle/Vessel Information Request printout; the written statement dated August 19, 2022 signed by RBRA Harbormaster James Malcolm concerning the ownership of Vessel 1; and the Statement of Ownership dated February 27, 2024 and the Affidavit of Ownership executed by Mr. Malcolm on February 26, 2025 concerning Vessel 2.

4. DBW's approval, voucher, warrant, or State Controller payment records for any claim in item 1, and any DBW review notes or correspondence with RBRA concerning either vessel.

5. All correspondence between DBW and RBRA, the County of Marin, or MarinLink mentioning "5286 TX," "5286TX," "Starfire," Holly Wild, "3944 TZ," "3944TZ," Moyer, "floating home," or the Vessel Buy-Back Program.

If any responsive claim categorized either vessel as abandoned rather than surrendered, please include the title-search and notice records required by Harbors and Navigation Code section 526. If no claim was submitted for either vessel, please say so in writing.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson
